Excellent — let’s make this hands-on, beginner-friendly guide to create a Trello dashboard with meaningful examples for team task management.

  2. Add lists and cards (tasks)

  4. Use dashboards, automation, and Power-Ups to visualize progress

🧭 Step-by-Step Guide: Creating a Trello Dashboard

🧩 Step 1: Sign in & Create a Workspace

  1. Go to 👉 https://trello.com

  2. Click Sign Up (or Log In if you already have an account).

  3. Use your Google or Microsoft account to sign in.

  4. Once logged in, click Create Workspace → give it a name.

    Example:

    yaml
    Workspace Name: ItTechGenie Projects
Purpose: Manage software training and course content creation

🗂 Step 2: Create a New Board

  1. Inside your workspace, click Create new board.

  2. Choose a board name, background color, and visibility.

    Example:

    yaml
    Board Name: Website Launch Project
Background: Blue or gradient theme
Visibility: Workspace (so your team can access it)

    ✅ This board will be your main dashboard for tracking all project activities.

📋 Step 3: Create Lists (Columns)

Lists act as stages of work — like Kanban columns.

List NamePurpose
🧠 BacklogStore new ideas or pending tasks
🚧 In ProgressTasks currently being worked on
✅ CompletedFinished tasks
📅 ReviewTasks that need approval or QA
🏁 DoneFully completed & verified

To add a list → click Add another list → type the name → press Enter.

🪶 Step 4: Add Cards (Tasks)

Each card represents a task or subproject.

Example cards:

ListCard (Task)Description
BacklogCreate UI wireframesInitial mockups for the new website
In ProgressDevelop landing pageFront-end React + Tailwind development
ReviewReview SEO planCheck keywords, title tags
DoneDeploy websiteFinal deployment to production server

To add a card:

  • Click Add a card under a list

  • Give it a title and press Enter

  • Click the card to open details:

    • Add a description

    • Attach files (mockups, docs)

    • Add checklists (subtasks)

    • Add due date

👥 Step 5: Assign Members to Tasks

  1. Open any card.

  2. Click Members on the right side.

  3. Choose team members (they must be part of the workspace).

Example Assignments:

TaskAssigned To
Create UI wireframesPriya (UI/UX)
Develop landing pageGopinath (Frontend)
Review SEO planDivya (Marketing)
Deploy websiteRamesh (DevOps)

🎨 Step 6: Use Labels to Categorize Tasks

Labels help visually identify task types or priorities.

Example Labels:

  • 🟢 Low Priority

  • 🟡 Medium Priority

  • 🔴 High Priority

  • 💡 Feature

  • 🐞 Bug Fix

  • 📢 Marketing

To add:
Open a card → Click Labels → choose color & name.

⏰ Step 7: Set Due Dates & Reminders

  1. Open a card → click Dates

  2. Set Start Date and Due Date

  3. Enable Remind me 1 day before

This keeps everyone on schedule.

✅ Step 8: Add Checklists for Subtasks

You can break a task into smaller actionable items.

Example (for “Develop Landing Page”)

Checklist name: “Development Tasks”

  • Setup React project

  • Design Hero Section

  • Integrate API

  • Test responsiveness

  • Final code review

Progress bar automatically shows how many items are done.

🧠 Step 9: Enable Dashboard View (Power-Up)

To visualize your project status:

  1. Click Views → Dashboard (top-right corner)

  2. You’ll see:

    • Task count per list

    • Tasks per member

    • Due-date distribution

  3. You can also use Calendar View or Timeline View for deadlines.

⚙️ Step 10: Automate Repetitive Tasks (Automation / Butler)

Trello includes Butler Automation.

Examples:

  • Move card to “Done” when all checklist items are complete

  • Send Slack message when a new card is added

  • Assign due date automatically when moved to “In Progress”

To set up:
Click Automation → Rules → Create rule
Example rule:

pgsql
When a card is moved to "In Progress",
set due date to 3 days in the future,
add member "Gopinath",
and apply label "High Priority".

📊 Step 11: Use Trello Dashboard for Reporting

Dashboard View allows you to track metrics like:

MetricExample
Tasks completed18
Tasks in progress5
Overdue tasks2
Top performerPriya (7 tasks completed)

You can present this during team meetings or export data to Excel (via Power-Ups).

🧭 Step 12: Best Practices

  • Keep card titles short and meaningful.

  • Always add descriptions and attachments.

  • Update status daily to keep dashboard fresh.

  • Use filters to view cards by member, label, or due date.

  • Conduct weekly review meetings using the dashboard.

🧩 Example Real-World Use Case

Scenario:

Board: “Python Bootcamp Launch”
Lists:

  • In Progress

  • Review

  • Marketing

  • Completed

Cards:

  • Design course syllabus → assigned to Gopinath

  • Record Module 1 videos → Priya

  • Upload to LMS → Ramesh

  • Create promotional poster → Divya

  • Post on Instagram → Marketing Team

Result:
Each department sees its workload, management sees overall progress, and the dashboard view shows completion trends.

# 🧭 Step-by-Step Guide: Creating a Trello Dashboard

---

## 🧩 Step 1: Sign in & Create a Workspace

1. Go to 👉 [https://trello.com](https://trello.com)
2. Click **Sign Up** (or **Log In** if you already have an account)
3. Use your **Google or Microsoft** account to sign in.
4. Once logged in, click **Create Workspace** → give it a name.

**Example:**

Workspace Name: ItTechGenie Projects
Purpose: Manage software training and course content creation

yaml

---

## 🗂 Step 2: Create a New Board

1. Inside your workspace, click **Create new board**.
2. Choose a **board name**, background color, and visibility.

**Example:**

Board Name: Website Launch Project
Background: Blue or gradient theme
Visibility: Workspace (so your team can access it)

yaml

✅ This board will be your **main dashboard** for tracking all project activities.

---

## 📋 Step 3: Create Lists (Columns)

Lists act as **stages of work** — like Kanban columns.

| List Name | Purpose |
|------------|----------|
| 🧠 Backlog | Store new ideas or pending tasks |
| 🚧 In Progress | Tasks currently being worked on |
| ✅ Completed | Finished tasks |
| 📅 Review | Tasks that need approval or QA |
| 🏁 Done | Fully completed & verified |

To add a list → click **Add another list** → type the name → press Enter.

---

## 🪶 Step 4: Add Cards (Tasks)

Each **card** represents a **task or subproject**.

| List | Card (Task) | Description |
|------|--------------|--------------|
| Backlog | Create UI wireframes | Initial mockups for the new website |
| In Progress | Develop landing page | Front-end React + Tailwind development |
| Review | Review SEO plan | Check keywords, title tags |
| Done | Deploy website | Final deployment to production server |

**To add a card:**
- Click **Add a card** under a list
- Give it a title and press Enter
- Click the card to open details:
  - Add a **description**
  - Attach files (mockups, docs)
  - Add **checklists** (subtasks)
  - Add **due date**

---

## 👥 Step 5: Assign Members to Tasks

1. Open any card.
2. Click **Members** on the right side.
3. Choose team members (they must be part of the workspace).

| Task | Assigned To |
|------|--------------|
| Create UI wireframes | Priya (UI/UX) |
| Develop landing page | Gopinath (Frontend) |
| Review SEO plan | Divya (Marketing) |
| Deploy website | Ramesh (DevOps) |

---

## 🎨 Step 6: Use Labels to Categorize Tasks

Labels help visually identify task types or priorities.

**Example Labels:**
- 🟢 Low Priority
- 🟡 Medium Priority
- 🔴 High Priority
- 💡 Feature
- 🐞 Bug Fix
- 📢 Marketing

**To add:**
Open a card → Click **Labels** → choose color & name.

---

## ⏰ Step 7: Set Due Dates & Reminders

1. Open a card → click **Dates**
2. Set **Start Date** and **Due Date**
3. Enable **Remind me 1 day before**

This keeps everyone on schedule.

---

## ✅ Step 8: Add Checklists for Subtasks

Break a task into smaller actionable items.

**Example (for “Develop Landing Page”):**

Checklist name: “Development Tasks”

- [ ] Setup React project
- [ ] Design Hero Section
- [ ] Integrate API
- [ ] Test responsiveness
- [ ] Final code review

Progress bar automatically shows how many items are done.

---

## 🧠 Step 9: Enable Dashboard View (Power-Up)

To visualize your project status:

1. Click **Views → Dashboard** (top-right corner)
2. You’ll see:
   - Task count per list
   - Tasks per member
   - Due-date distribution
3. You can also use **Calendar View** or **Timeline View** for deadlines.

---

## ⚙️ Step 10: Automate Repetitive Tasks (Automation / Butler)

Trello includes **Butler Automation**.

Examples:
- Move card to “Done” when all checklist items are complete
- Send Slack message when a new card is added
- Assign due date automatically when moved to “In Progress”

**To set up:**
Click **Automation → Rules → Create rule**

Example rule:

When a card is moved to "In Progress",
set due date to 3 days in the future,
add member "Gopinath",
and apply label "High Priority".

yaml

---

## 📊 Step 11: Use Trello Dashboard for Reporting

Dashboard View allows you to track metrics like:

| Metric | Example |
|---------|----------|
| Tasks completed | 18 |
| Tasks in progress | 5 |
| Overdue tasks | 2 |
| Top performer | Priya (7 tasks completed) |

You can present this during team meetings or export data to Excel (via Power-Ups).

---

## 🧭 Step 12: Best Practices

- Keep card titles short and meaningful.
- Always add **descriptions** and **attachments**.
- Update status daily to keep dashboard fresh.
- Use **filters** to view cards by member, label, or due date.
- Conduct **weekly review meetings** using the dashboard.

---

## 🧩 Example Real-World Use Case

**Scenario:**
An *IT Training Company* is planning a new online course launch.

**Board:** “Python Bootcamp Launch”
**Lists:**
- Backlog
- In Progress
- Review
- Marketing
- Completed

**Cards:**
- Design course syllabus → assigned to *Gopinath*
- Record Module 1 videos → *Priya*
- Upload to LMS → *Ramesh*
- Create promotional poster → *Divya*
- Post on Instagram → *Marketing Team*

**Result:**
Each department sees its workload, management sees overall progress, and the dashboard view shows completion trends.

---

✅ End of Trello Dashboard Setup Guide
